simple: Animation capture lets you make animations by acting them out instead of posing every frame by hand. With Face capture, your webcam copies your facial expressions onto a character with an animation-ready head. With Body capture, you upload a short video of a person moving and Roblox turns it into a full-body animation for an R15 rig. Both create real keyframes you can tweak afterward, save, and publish.
analogy: It is like a motion-capture studio for movies, where an actor's real movements are copied onto a digital character, except you only need a webcam or a phone video.
keyPoints: Both tools are beta features, so you must turn them on in Studio's beta features first.

Face capture: open the Clip Editor from the Avatar tab, select a rig with an animation-compatible head, name the animation, click Face Capture, accept the consent popup, then press the red circle to record.
Face recordings can be up to 60 seconds. Stop with the red square or timer, and click Re-Record to try again.
For good face capture, use a well-lit room and keep your face in the center of the camera view.
Body capture: select an R15 rig, click the three-dot button, then Import, then Live Animation Creator, and choose an `.mp4` or `.mov` video.
Body videos need one well-lit person visible the whole time, one continuous shot under 15 seconds, a steady camera, and must follow Roblox's Community Rules and Terms of Use.
After capture, you can fine-tune keyframes, save, and export the animation like any other.

terms.animation capture: Making an animation by recording real movement instead of posing by hand.
terms.puppeteer: To control a character's movements with your own, like a puppet copying you.
terms.animation compatible head: A character head built to move its face, so it can smile, blink, or drop its jaw.
terms.keyframe: A saved pose at a moment in time. Capture makes these for you automatically.
terms.R15 rig: Roblox's standard 15-part character body, with joints for arms, legs, and torso.
terms.beta feature: A new feature still being tested. You turn it on yourself in Studio's beta features settings.
terms.consent: Saying yes on purpose. The Face Capture popup asks if you agree to your face movements being collected and your camera being used.
terms.NPC: Non-player character, a character controlled by the game instead of a person.

watchOut: Not enabling the beta feature first. The capture buttons will not be available.
Recording in a dark room or off-center. The camera has trouble tracking you; get good light and center your face.
Uploading a video with more than one person, camera cuts, shaky camera, or longer than 15 seconds. Keep it to one person, one steady shot, under 15 seconds.
Using face capture on a rig without an animation-compatible head. Pick a rig with a dynamic head.
